rv.q: Though focused on the central performance it’s an ensemble affair, the cast mingling with the audience on arrival, handing out mince pies and satsumas, and later cheerfully doubling and tripling roles and ringing out hymns on handbells. The masterful set and costumes are by Rob Howell.
The glorious thing about Christmas traditions is that we do not see them forming, yet once they are established we warmly acknowledge their annual appearance.

This exceptional version of A Christmas Carol remains a magical festive experience. … Simm… brings a sardonic and acerbic level of humour not seen in the role before and this gives more levity to the show overall.

This time it’s the turn of John Simm. Over the years, this show – which transferred to Broadway, toured the US and was also staged in Melbourne – has raised about £1.5 million globally for food poverty charities.
